instruction: Use both R5 arms to pick up the two assigned objects: the physical left arm with the white wrist camera grasps the tennis ball on its black support; the physical right arm with the black wrist camera grasps the upright red cola can. Lift each object a small visible distance from its support, verify that both remain held, then keep powered hold. Coordinate simultaneous motion only when both approach paths are visibly clear and separated.
content: This is one coordinated bimanual task. The three images are physical left wrist (left), physical right wrist (right), and shared global view (top). Target identity and clearance come primarily from the shared global view. Keep each arm in its own approach corridor. The operator reports manually trying the work areas without collision and is attending. No measured transform between the bases or geometric collision certificate is available.

At setup the tennis ball is to the right and ahead of the left gripper in the global view. The red cola can is to the left and ahead of the right gripper. The other bottle at the back of the table is not a target. Recheck current geometry; objects, tools, cables, papers, wrist cameras and the black ball support are obstacles. Preserve independent base frames: screen-right is not base +Y. The earlier left-arm run repeatedly moved the wrong way with +Y; local -Y previously brought the ball toward the wrist finger corridor, but the arm posture changed after stopping. Verify local response afresh; do not transfer signs from one arm to the other.

Use original GPT-Policy paired targets and fresh observation feedback. Start with bounded contact-free corrections to verify each arm response; once both directions and clear swept corridors are supported, command both in the same move_to or move_eef_chunk. The host preflights both selected sides and synchronizes segment durations by slowing. Numeric path checks do not certify collision clearance. Null holds the unselected side. Gripper actions are separate from arm paths. A hand that is not yet aligned must continue approaching rather than close just because the other hand is ready.

Both grippers increase raw position to open; 4.8 is the left tested opening target and a nominal same-model transfer on the right. Endpoints and 8 cm fingertip offsets are approximate, not force or width measurements. When the empty right gripper is opened, inspect the actual right-wrist and global result before approaching. Close in separate bounded increments only when the target sits between the inner finger surfaces at sufficient depth in both views. Avoid tipping or deforming the cola can. Neither finger motion nor motor stall proves grasp.

Use the global image for remaining approach gap, height and placement; wrist centering alone is insufficient. Inspect actual J1..J6 motion, command poses, residuals and recent visual progress for each arm. Small accepted tracking discrepancies do not require exact-zero correction, but unintended direction or loss of clearance requires handoff. A successful grasp must show the assigned object leaving its support and remaining retained in fresh images. done requires both objects lifted; keep holding afterward without homing or opening. No previous run has proved this paired task successful.

The preceding paired trial on 2026-09-27 executed 15 approach actions, including simultaneous left/right paths. Left -Y and right +Y brought their respective targets toward the wrist finger corridors; +X advanced both arms. The right empty gripper was physically opened to raw command 4.8 with measured feedback about 4.697, confirmed in images. Neither arm closed on or lifted an object. That trial stopped because a small secondary joint component reversed about 0.17 degrees despite useful net progress and less than one degree endpoint error. The timed-path host now permits an absolute reverse deadband of 0.3 degrees while still requiring aggregate progress, stable feedback and the existing residual bounds. Stopping released both arms and changed their postures, especially the right wrist orientation. Use fresh command poses as references and reassess image responses; do not replay prior absolute poses. A target outside the current wrist image is not gone: locate it in the fresh global image and choose a supported contact-free viewing/approach correction. Image up/down does not by itself determine physical height; distinguish forward gap from height by observed responses and the global scene.

A later attempt, dual-policy-9de9db4b3d4f segment 7, closed both jaws too early: the targets were horizontally near the wrist-image center but still ahead of the fingertips; the ball was also above the effective contact region. Four closures to normalized opening 0.2 and a lift did not pick up either object. Then advancing closed jaws did not correct the missing insertion depth. Do not repeat this pattern. If fresh views confirm an empty grasp, first reopen for clearance using gripper_open_step_limit_normalized relative to gripper_command_normalized, then align height and fore-aft depth with open fingers. The external camera can be occluded by the wrist bodies; occlusion is not contact evidence. Reassess left and right independently and close only the ready side. A rejected opening from 0.2 to 0.4 exceeded the 0.1 raw opening increment; the preview-copy error falsely said the session was latched, although both live backends remained healthy. Smaller opening increments can proceed. Current feedback and images remain authoritative; no previous run has demonstrated either object lifted in this paired setup.

The most recent failed run, dual-policy-331fc4c636dd, ended at segment 8 after repeated closures and short lifts. Final commanded normalized openings were left 0.02 and right 0.05. Fresh wrist images after the run still showed the ball outside the closed left finger corridor and the closed right fingertips in front of the can; both objects remained on their supports. The earlier statements that the fingers surrounded the objects were model judgments contradicted by these images, not measured contact. Arm motions completed with roughly 1.2-1.3 degree residuals; that successful execution did not establish a grasp. Do not treat another closure or another lift as a remedy for an empty grasp. If a lift fails to carry the object and no contact is established, reopen within the reported opening bounds and correct lateral alignment, contact height and insertion depth with fresh global and wrist observations before closing again. A target merely ahead of the fingertips is not enclosed. The new host opens both empty grippers before this run; verify that visual opening first. The trajectory envelope is now 24 degrees per joint and 33 degrees joint norm; use longer clear approach paths where supported, but do not enlarge near-object moves solely because the limit is larger. No prior paired grasp has been verified.

Restart update at 2026-09-27 16:02: the operator moved the objects closer and requested a fresh attempt. Run dual-policy-b70644bdf95d ended during reopening after unverified lifts; both objects remained supported. Its right gripper did open (raw feedback 1.9669 to 2.0657, command 2.1510), but held joints did not meet the settle stability window. This was not proof of a gripper stall or grasp. Both arms subsequently released and returned to low postures, with empty, partly open fingers. Current images and feedback supersede all earlier absolute targets and object positions. Approach the newly placed tennis ball and red container from the freshly observed pose; confirm insertion depth and height independently for each side before closing. The host will finish opening the empty jaws first. No successful grasp or lift is established.
